content.value_statement: Multi-cloud planning is hard when teams must compare AWS, Azure, and GCP under real constraints. This skill guides architecture choices, migration planning, and cost tradeoffs.
actual_capabilities: Compares equivalent compute, storage, database, and caching services across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
Recommends multi-cloud patterns such as disaster recovery, best-of-breed services, and geographic distribution.
Explains cloud-agnostic architecture layers using Kubernetes, Terraform, open databases, and portable observability tools.
Outlines phased migration steps from assessment through optimization.
Highlights cost optimization tactics across reserved capacity, spot usage, right-sizing, data transfer, and tagging.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance, not live pricing or provider availability data.
It does not create Terraform modules, deployment pipelines, or cloud accounts.
It cannot replace a formal security, compliance, or financial review.
It focuses on AWS, Azure, and GCP rather than niche or regional cloud providers.

use_cases.title: Plan a Resilient Cloud Strategy
use_cases.description: Select a primary cloud and disaster recovery target while documenting failover, replication, and recovery assumptions.

use_cases.title: Compare Services for a New Platform
use_cases.description: Map workload needs to comparable services across AWS, Azure, and GCP before choosing provider-specific components.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Migration Roadmap
use_cases.description: Break a cloud migration into assessment, pilot, migration, and optimization phases with practical validation points.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Cloud Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare AWS, Azure, and GCP services for this workload: [describe workload]. Include compute, storage, database, and monitoring choices.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Multi-Cloud Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a multi-cloud pattern for [business goal]. Include benefits, tradeoffs, failure modes, and when to avoid the pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Migration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased migration plan from [current cloud] to [target cloud or multi-cloud model]. Include dependencies, pilot scope, risks, and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Enterprise Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this proposed multi-cloud architecture: [architecture summary]. Assess portability, cost, operations, security, resilience, and provider lock-in.

output_examples.input: Design a disaster recovery approach for an application currently running on AWS.
output_examples.output: A primary AWS deployment with warm standby on Azure, cross-cloud database replication, automated failover tests, and documented recovery objectives.

output_examples.input: Compare cloud choices for a portable container platform.
output_examples.output: A Kubernetes-based design using EKS, AKS, or GKE, plus Terraform, PostgreSQL, Redis, Prometheus, and cloud-neutral deployment conventions.

output_examples.input: Plan a migration from one cloud provider to a multi-cloud operating model.
output_examples.output: A four-phase roadmap covering inventory, pilot workload selection, incremental migration, dual-run validation, monitoring, and cost optimization.

best_practices: Start with workload goals, compliance needs, resilience targets, and team operating capacity.
Use portable foundations such as Terraform, Kubernetes, open databases, and standard observability tools where practical.
Document provider-specific choices, failover procedures, cost assumptions, and operational ownership.
anti_patterns: Do not use multiple clouds only for appearance without a clear business or resilience reason.
Do not assume every managed service has a direct equivalent across providers.
Do not design cross-cloud data flows without modeling latency, egress costs, and compliance requirements.

faq.question: Which cloud providers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on AWS, Azure, and GCP, with service comparisons and architecture patterns across those providers.

faq.question: Can it generate working infrastructure code?
faq.answer: No. It gives architecture guidance and implementation considerations, but it does not generate tested Terraform modules.

faq.question: Does it use current cloud pricing?
faq.answer: No. It discusses pricing factors and cost strategies, but live pricing should be checked with provider calculators.

faq.question: Is this useful for disaster recovery planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a pattern for primary workloads in one cloud with disaster recovery in another cloud.

faq.question: Can it help reduce vendor lock-in?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends portable layers such as Kubernetes, Terraform, open databases, and cloud-neutral observability tools.

faq.question: Does it replace architecture review by cloud experts?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure decisions, but expert review is still needed for security, compliance, and production readiness.
